key_insight: Digital motor scores from wearable/phone-style assessments map onto distinct striatal dopamine-denervation patterns in Parkinson’s disease, especially for gait and balance.
clinical_relevance: The findings suggest digital health metrics could help quantify Parkinsonian motor dysfunction and potentially complement biomarker-based stratification in research settings.
method: 17 Parkinson’s disease patients and 39 healthy controls underwent simultaneous 11C-dMP-PET and resting-state fMRI.
Composite digital motor scores were derived for arm swing, gait, and balance from digital health technology parameters.
Voxel-based PET correlation analyses identified striatal clusters, followed by seed-based functional connectivity mapping.
evidence_signal: This was a small hybrid PET-MRI study with correlational analyses showing domain-specific associations between digital motor scores, dopamine transporter binding, and frontostriatal connectivity.
watch_item: The sample size was small and the results are preliminary, so external validation and prospective testing are needed before broader implementation.
paper_title: Striatal representations and network correlates of digital motor scores in Parkinsons disease
